question: New job: part NIST FTC-10 (Housing (NIST PMI test case FTC-10, public domain)), material 6061-T6 aluminum (assumed; drawing gives none), qty 1, 0 features, deepest pocket 31 mm, 0 holes, plate 118 cm2. Using ONLY Keewano history: (1) which toolpath strategies should the CAM search try first for this part (rank by simulated cycle time on the most similar past parts, especially by pocket depth; drop strategies that failed verification or never win), (2) which supplier to buy a missing aluminum blank from (delivered price vs lead days from past quotes), (3) which step of the order is the bottleneck (StepSeconds), (4) before vs after: agent programming time vs the manual estimate, best vs manual-baseline machine time. Then call final_decision.

answer.supplier_reason: Completed quote: 4760 cents ($47.60) delivered in 2 days, compared with Pacific Metals Supply at 8670 cents ($86.70) in 0 days. Saves $39.10 for a qty-1 job with no rush stated.
answer.before_after: Programming: the shop's manual estimate is 14400 s (4 h). The past FTC-10 job has no JobProgrammedSeconds recorded, so this uses the sum of its cam.* steps: 323 s (5:23). On similar pockets (SM-102, SM-106) JobProgrammedSeconds was 3 s. Machine time: baseline-manual took 6586 s (1:49:46) and failed 3 checks (leftover, rapid_into_stock, flat_plunge). The best verified program, adaptive-L2.5-D24-F0.5, took 1801 s (30:01), which is 72.7% less machine time.
answer.summary: Try adaptive-L2.5-D24-F0.5 first (1801 s, verified on the earlier 31 mm FTC-10 job), then adaptive-L2.5-D12-F0.4 (2071 s) and adaptive-L1.5-D12-F0.4 (2294 s). Skip baseline-manual, which failed 3 simulator checks. Buy the blank from Bay Alloy & Steel ($47.60, 2 days) rather than Pacific Metals ($86.70, same day). The slowest step is the supplier phone call (296 s), and programming takes about 5:23 compared with a 4 h manual estimate.
